correctness.rationale: For arbitrary interior a,b, direct disk-automorphism conjugation expresses b_a/b_b on the boundary as omega (1-delta t)/(1-delta conjugate(t)). The argument image of 1-delta T is exactly [-arcsin(delta),arcsin(delta)] and doubles to a closed centered arc. Complex coefficient supremum is then an exact cosine maximization, including the coincident-zero and complex-phase cases. The metric projection is the unique minimal enclosing-circle center, with distinct endpoint-chord (alpha<=pi/2) and antipodal (alpha>=pi/2) proofs; this also establishes equality cases and the orthogonality threshold. A standalone stdlib script reproduces 144 mesh checks with largest discrepancy 2.8566783e-07, but the analytic proof—not sampling—establishes the infinite/continuum assertion.

originality.rationale: The 2023 source arXiv:2306.02638 supplies general *qualitative* uniform-algebra and finite-Blaschke Birkhoff--James characterizations, and it covers the orthogonality criterion in principle after separate calculation of the arc. The present final claim is the *entire two-generator norm for every complex coefficient pair*, plus a unique quantitative best scalar and distance phase transition; these are not stated or directly supplied by the inspected source. Exact-formula and alias searches found no stronger source implying the full formula. A differently indexed or differently phrased prior computation remains a genuine possibility; unsuccessful search is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Elementary Blaschke factors are canonical degree-one building blocks for finite inner functions and are directly motivated by a published finite-Blaschke BJ investigation. The theorem supplies a natural complete complex two-generator norm invariant under disk-automorphism reduction, classifies the marked spans by one pseudohyperbolic parameter, and solves exact best one-dimensional approximation including a sharp transition and uniqueness. This is a complete norm-geometric classification rather than a single artificial coefficient evaluation or mere reformulation of qualitative BJ orthogonality. It does not claim a wider operator-theoretic consequence.
